name: select
description: One choice from a known list. A native `<select>`, deliberately: it gets the platform's own picker on a phone, works with a hardware keyboard and a screen reader without a line of JavaScript, and cannot be scrolled out of view. A custom listbox is only worth its cost when the options need to be more than text.

control.$description: `appearance:none` for the chrome, but the element stays a `<select>` — the picker, the keyboard model and the announcement are all the platform's.

marker.$description: `pointer-events:none` or the chevron eats the click that should open the picker.

a11y.note: A real `<label for>` and a real `<select>`, so the name, role and value are all announced without help. The chevron is decorative and `aria-hidden`. Keep the control at least 2.75rem: the whole box is the target, and the chevron alone is well under 24px.
